correctness.rationale: Every 3-periodic state of connected GH dynamics is either all resting or a globally phase-rotating ternary coloring. The latter is equivalent to the local successor-neighbor condition. The bipartite incidence-mask bijection is disjoint and exhaustive, and two independent integer enumerations across 3^(m-1) point assignments agree on all three graphs (m=8,9,10) and a separate direct 729-state check verifies the rule on K3,3. Computation asserts each count. No infinite-domain claim is inferred from finite tests.

value.rationale: These three canonical cubic Levi incidence graphs are natural finite symmetric excitable networks, not parameter-picked slices. Their exact surviving primitive three-wave counts quantify persistent phase-coherent excitation and supply three reproducible benchmark invariants for studies of propagation on historically important 8_3, 9_3, and 10_3 configurations. Numerical answers are nonobvious and not supplied by qualitative winding criteria; no downstream general theorem is claimed.
